Let the bottom-left pocket \(D\) be \((0,0)\). Counting the grid squares, the board has dimensions \(10\times 8\), so
\[
P=(4,0),\qquad A=(10,0),\qquad C=(0,8),\qquad B=(10,8).
\]

1. After bouncing at \(P\), the ball travels upward and to the right with slope
   \[
   \tan\theta=\frac12.
   \]
   To reach the right wall, it travels \(10-4=6\) squares horizontally, rising
   \[
   \frac12\cdot 6=3
   \]
   squares. Thus it first hits the right wall at \((10,3)\).

2. The ball then reflects upward and to the left. To reach the top edge, it must rise \(8-3=5\) squares, requiring a horizontal movement of
   \[
   \frac{5}{1/2}=10
   \]
   squares to the left.

3. Starting from \(x=10\), moving \(10\) squares left takes it to \(x=0\). Hence it arrives at the top-left corner, Pocket \(C\).

\[
\boxed{\text{C: Pocket C}}
\]
